subject: Renewal & capacity escalation — proposal for 32 GPU reserved pool
messages:
From: Ellie Thompson <ellie@nebula-ai.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@nebula-ai.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase request

Jordan —

Our current reserved pool (16 GPUs) is up for renewal on June 15. Over the last quarter our inference usage has steadily grown and we’d like to explore a renewal that doubles reserved capacity to 32 GPUs starting at contract renewal. High-level asks: 

- Pricing: revised per-hour reserved rate for 32-GPU commit (please show line-item comparison vs current 16-GPU rate).
- Ramp: a transition plan (staged ramp or immediate cutover) and any pro-rating for partial-month moves.
- Throughput/SLA: we need a throughput guarantee for our baseline model serving (p95 generation latency target and sustained throughput for our peak windows).
- Ops: rollback/fallback plan if capacity is constrained and a fallback to compatible model variant.

I’ve attached the latest SOW with expected throughput numbers and our renewal contact list (Nebula_SOW_v2.pdf). Procurement will need an indicative commercial term sheet and the list of required SOC/compliance artifacts.

Can you put together an initial proposal and pricing? We’re aiming to finalize before the renewal date.

Thanks,
Ellie Thompson
VP Product — Nebula AI
ellie@nebula-ai.com

Attachment: Nebula_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Thompson <ellie@nebula-ai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase request

Ellie —

Thanks for the clear ask and the SOW — this is great context. Quick confirmation: we can absolutely support a 32-GPU reserved pool for your workload. I’ll pull together a concise term sheet that compares the current 16-GPU economics to a 32-GPU commit and outline a recommended ramp schedule.

Where we are planning to focus in the proposal:
- Per-hour reserved rate (committed) vs on-demand burst rates.
- Suggested ramp: 4‑week staged ramp (16 -> 24 -> 32) with pro-rated billing at the milestone month, or an immediate cutover with a one-time onboarding credit.
- Throughput SLOs: propose credits if p95 latency or sustained throughput commitments are missed (we’ll include a clear SLA credit table).
- Operational runbook: handoff to Customer Success for rollout, and SE-driven capacity validation prior to full traffic migration.

Looping in Ben (SE) and Lauren (Revenue Ops) to model the throughput guarantees and finalize finance-friendly billing language. I’ll attach a draft term sheet shortly.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Attachment: (term sheet coming)

Subject: Fwd: Renewal + capacity increase request — SE sizing notes

Sharing quick sizing and risk items for the proposed 32-GPU reserved pool. Forwarding Jordan’s note with inline comments.

Key technical considerations: 
- Baseline: current models average 80ms per token on our profile tests at your reported sequence lengths; sustained throughput at 16 GPUs has headroom ~1.8x during offpeak but approaches saturation in your top 2 peak hours.
- Suggested guaranteed baseline: define a sustained concurrency target (e.g., sustained 400 concurrent inference streams @ given seq lengths) rather than raw tokens/sec; we can map that to an SLO and measurable metrics in the Console.
- Ramp plan: recommended staged ramp to validate KV cache warming and prefix caching benefits — suggest 2-week validation windows at 24 GPUs before final cutover to 32.
- Failure/fallback: automatic routing to a compatible quantized variant with a specified QoS delta (e.g., ~3–6% quality delta) if health checks fail — document and communicate to Nebula.

Provisional numbers (ballpark):
- Current committed rate (16 GPUs): $7.25 / GPU / hr
- Proposed 32-GPU committed rate (volume-discount tier): $5.95 / GPU / hr (12-month term) — includes 10% onboarding credit in month 1 if ramped over first 30 days.

I’ll prepare the validation checklist for the Migration Plan once Jordan confirms which ramp option Nebula prefers.

—Ben
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: 12-mo renewal + 32-GPU reserved expansion (draft commercial terms)

Ellie / Marcus —

Appended is our formal draft for the renewal and capacity escalation. Summary highlights (full term sheet attached): Redwood_TermSheet_32GPU.xlsx

1) Capacity & term
- Committed capacity: 32 x A100-class GPUs (reserved pool)
- Commitment term: 12 months from date of activation
- Ramp option A (recommended): staged over 4 weeks (16 -> 24 -> 32). Option B: immediate activation to 32.

2) Pricing (committed reserved rate)
- 32-GPU reserved rate: $5.95 / GPU / hour (applies to all committed instances during the term)
- Current 16-GPU legacy rate for comparison: $7.25 / GPU / hour
- Onboarding credit: 10% of the first-month committed spend if staged ramp used and validation checklist completed.

3) Throughput & SLOs
- Measurables: p95 generation latency and sustained concurrency for production model as defined in the attached validation checklist.
- Financial remedy: service credits up to 10% of monthly committed invoice if monthly p95 latency SLO breached more than two separate measurement windows in a billing month.

4) Billing & proration
- Month of activation will be pro-rated by hour for any partial-month change.
- Early term change (downscale within first 90 days) is allowed with a one-time adjustment fee equal to two weeks of committed spend unless Nebula elects staged ramping which waives the fee.

5) Compliance & next steps
- We will provide SOC2 report and standard evidence items within 5 business days after NDA/PO receipt.
- Ask: please confirm preferred ramp option and we’ll get a final term sheet and an MSA addendum ready for signature.

I’ve attached the draft term sheet. If this is directionally aligned, Lauren will run final pricing and procurement language and I’ll schedule a 30-min alignment call (SE + Success) to lock the migration checklist.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_TermSheet_32GPU.xlsx (xlsx)

If you can take the pricing concession to Finance and return a final term sheet, we’ll aim to get PO approval within two weeks.
